pathway.title: Somnigroup International Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Scale and channel breadth are real strengths but are being diluted by lower-margin acquired earnings. The group has four segments, direct sales of 54.44% of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 and no customer above 5% of global sales before Leggett & Platt, which spreads demand risk across stores, wholesale partners and now components. Leggett & Platt earns a gross margin of 17.71% against 42.02% for the group, so each acquired dollar of sales carries less margin to service debt. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 35–36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C11

Cash generation is the strongest support. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 931.3 million less capital expenditure of USD 232.6 million leaves free cash flow of USD 698.7 million, 0.55x trailing EBITDA, and dividends of USD 108.1 million in nine months 2026 took 16.44% of nine-month free cash flow. Capital expenditure and the dividend are the levers management controls, so the cash flow can protect creditors in a downturn if they are used. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44; calculation C2

Leverage is the weakest dimension, and the range of credible answers is wide. Reported total debt to EBITDA is 4.25x and net debt to EBITDA 3.77x, also 3.77x pro forma for the USD 200.0 million Term B prepayment of 2026-10-01, while the issuer's covenant ratio is 2.69x. The reported figures overstate leverage because Leggett & Platt's debt is counted against 36 days of its earnings; the covenant ratio understates it because its EBITDA is 34.23% above adjusted EBITDA, and no source gives a full-period figure between the two. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54; calculation C1; calculation C6

Liquidity and the debt calendar are comfortable for the next two years. Liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million is made of USD 612.1 million of cash, USD 412.1 million after the USD 200.0 million prepayment of 2026-10-01, and USD 1,182.7 million of revolver availability; it covers the 2027 maturities 2.99 times. The bank debt now matures in 2031, so the next test of market access is the USD 500.0 million Leggett & Platt note due 2027-11-15 and the securitization due 2027-10-07. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 47; calculation C3

Interest cost is likely to rise as a share of cash flow, and a rising rate would add to it. The issuer's guide of about USD 240 million of cash interest for 2026 implies USD 68.5 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 57.17 million in the first three, and 43.11% of principal is floating rate, so 100 bp costs about USD 24.3 million a year, 3.48% of trailing free cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 47, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C7

Earnings momentum is negative and is the main reason the credit is stretched. Net sales excluding Leggett & Platt fell 6.80% in the third quarter of 2026, pro forma net sales including it fell 6.30%, and adjusted operating income excluding it fell 5.91%, with Mattress Firm and North America each down 5.8% and International down 12.3%. A fixed cost base of stores, plants and leases, of which operating lease cost alone was USD 489.5 million in FY2025, turns that fall into a larger fall in EBITDA, which is why interest cover and leverage are sensitive to a further weak quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 34–36, 49–51; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C5; calculation C10

Financial policy is acquisitive and the equity cushion is thin, so creditor protection rests on restraint rather than structure. Total debt rose USD 1,571.7 million, 41.25%, since 2024-12-31, goodwill and intangibles exceed stockholders' equity so tangible equity is negative USD 2,974.8 million, and the unsecured share of principal rose to 55.09% with USD 1,500.0 million of Leggett & Platt notes that carry no guarantee. No sponsor exists to inject equity, and the guarantors are not named, so the priority of the new debt against the older creditors is not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C4

cells.text: Designs, manufactures, distributes and retails bedding (mattresses, foundations, adjustable bases, pillows) under Tempur-Pedic, Sealy, Stearns & Foster, Mattress Firm and Dreams; since 2026-08-26 it also makes engineered components (innersprings, specialty foam, adjustable-bed mechanisms, automotive and industrial products) through Leggett & Platt
Four: Mattress Firm (retail), Leggett & Platt (components), Tempur Sealy North America and Tempur Sealy International; Q3 2026 net sales shares are 42.89%, 15.85%, 29.48% and 11.77%

FY2025 direct 63.48% (4,745.9) and wholesale 36.52% (2,730.6) of net sales against 24.93% direct in FY2024; Q3 2026 direct bedding 54.44% (1,279.8), wholesale bedding and furnishings 41.25% (969.7) and specialized products 4.31% (101.3)
Wholesale partners with more than 20,000 doors; no customer above 5% of global sales after Mattress Firm and before Leggett & Platt; Leggett & Platt customer concentration not stated
2,875 company-owned stores at 2026-09-30, of which 2,152 are Mattress Firm (2,852 and 2,174 at 2025-12-31); 62 Mattress Firm distribution centers
Over 70 manufacturing facilities and four research and development facilities before Leggett & Platt; Leggett & Platt adds about 100 manufacturing facilities in 19 countries

Tempur Sealy North America sold 976.3 to Mattress Firm in FY2025 (26.55% of its sales including inter-segment) and 315.2 in Q3 2026 (31.26%); eliminated on consolidation; a regulatory commitment sets 43% of premium floor slots for third-party mattresses
Q3 2026 net sales 1,868.7 in the United States (79.49%) and 482.1 elsewhere; sales in over 100 countries
FY2025 cost of sales 57.4%, selling and marketing 23.3% and general, administrative and other 9.3% of net sales; operating lease cost 489.5 (6.55% of net sales)

Chemicals, additives, textiles, steel and foam from third parties under supply agreements, no single long-term vendor dependency stated; commodity volatility affects profitability; most U.S. sales are of U.S.-made product
Modest, with sales generally lower in the second and fourth quarters; securitization availability varies with receivables seasonality
More than 20,000 before Leggett & Platt; Leggett & Platt headcount not stated

runs.text: The first strength is cash generation. Trailing free cash flow of USD 698.7 million, 0.55x EBITDA, is large enough to fund the dividend of USD 108.1 million and net repayment of USD 583.9 million of credit facilities in nine months, so deleveraging does not depend on market access. This lowers refinancing risk but is only as durable as sales. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44; calculation C2

The second strength is liquidity and tenor. Liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million covers the USD 600.5 million due in 2027 2.99 times, and the bank facilities run to 2031, so a failed refinancing of the 2027 items would not force a liquidity crisis. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 47; calculation C3

The third strength is scale and channel breadth: four segments, brands across price points, direct sales of 54.44% of the third quarter, and no customer above 5% of global sales before Leggett & Platt, which spreads demand risk and supports pricing. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C11

The first weakness is leverage on reported earnings, 4.25x total debt to EBITDA, with the full-period figure not printed; it limits headroom for a downturn or another acquisition. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1

The second weakness is falling underlying sales, down 6.80% in the third quarter excluding Leggett & Platt, with fixed store and plant costs that magnify the fall in EBITDA and so raise leverage and lower cover. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 34–36; calculation C5

The third weakness is earnings quality and integration: add-backs are 16.16% of adjusted EBITDA in the quarter and the covenant measure adds USD 475.5 million, including USD 145.0 million of unrealised savings, so reported compliance is a weak signal of cash earnings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation C6

The fourth weakness is structure and policy: the unsecured share of principal is 55.09%, USD 1,500.0 million of notes sit at Leggett & Platt without guarantees, guarantors are not named and tangible equity is negative USD 2,974.8 million, so priority and loss absorption for lenders are not established. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C8; calculation C9

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The two acquisitions since 2025-02-05 define the credit. Mattress Firm closed on 2025-02-05 for total consideration of USD 5,408.4 million: USD 3,091.5 million of cash, USD 2,245.1 million of shares at USD 65.65 each and USD 71.8 million of settled pre-existing balances, less USD 267.0 million of cash acquired. The cash was funded by USD 625.0 million of the Delayed Draw Term A Loan, USD 679.5 million of revolver borrowing and about USD 1,592.0 million of Term B Loan proceeds released from escrow, where they had been held since 2024-10-24, and the same proceeds also repaid Mattress Firm's debt and paid fees. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93, 97; calculation C2

Leggett & Platt closed on 2026-08-26 for total consideration of USD 1,289.6 million, almost all in new shares valued at USD 64.09 each, with net consideration of USD 730.0 million after USD 560.2 million of cash acquired; its three senior notes of USD 500.0 million each remain outstanding at Leggett & Platt, Incorporated with no guarantee, and the debt assumed was recorded at USD 1,283.6 million. No new bonds were issued in either transaction. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17, 21–23; calculation C3

The financing around the second deal was a refinancing, not new money for the purchase. Amendment No. 5 of 2026-07-27 added a USD 1,200.0 million Term A Loan and USD 510.0 million of revolving commitments, took revolver commitments to USD 1,700.0 million, extended both to 2031-07-27, and repaid the earlier term loans, and USD 700.0 million of the Term B Loan was prepaid with the remaining proceeds. A further USD 200.0 million of the Term B Loan was prepaid on 2026-10-01 with cash acquired and cash from operations, after the balance-sheet date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 46

fields.value: Financial foundation for Somnigroup International Inc. (the consolidated group, formerly Tempur Sealy International, Inc.) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: income statement, cash flow statement, balance sheet, debt, leverage, interest cover, liquidity and constructed trailing periods in USD millions for FY2024, FY2025, the first nine months of 2025 and 2026 and the twelve months to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used and no web search was made. The run settings were read as the user's dated inputs, not as evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is 4.25x trailing reported EBITDA on USD 5,381.6 million of debt at 2026-09-30, overstated because Leggett & Platt's debt is set against only 36 days of its earnings, so creditors should rely on cash generation and liquidity until full-period earnings are printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's covenant leverage of 2.69x is lower by construction: it divides by USD 1,864.8 million of covenant EBITDA, which is USD 475.5 million above adjusted EBITDA and includes USD 145.0 million of expected cost savings. Free cash flow of USD 657.6 million in nine months 2026, cash interest cover of 5.01x and liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million support the credit, but net sales excluding Leggett & Platt fell 6.80% in the third quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage on reported earnings is high but overstated at the latest date, while the issuer's own ratio is understated by construction, so the credible range is wide. Total debt at carrying value rose from USD 3,809.9 million at 2024-12-31 to USD 4,685.7 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 5,381.6 million at 2026-09-30, as the Mattress Firm and Leggett & Platt acquisitions were financed with borrowing and new shares. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 4.53x, 4.51x and 4.25x at those dates, and net debt to EBITDA was 4.39x, 4.38x and 3.77x. The latest figures use trailing EBITDA of USD 1,264.9 million, up from USD 1,039.3 million, but that figure holds 36 days of Leggett & Platt against all of its debt, so a full-period ratio would be lower and no filing prints the earnings needed to say by how much. The USD 200.0 million Term B prepayment of 2026-10-01 lowers debt and cash equally, so pro forma net debt stays at USD 4,769.5 million and pro forma net leverage at 3.77x.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7, 19, 21, 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 63, 73; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The year-end 2024 ratios are not like for like either: debt includes the USD 1,600.0 million Term B Loan held in escrow ahead of the Mattress Firm closing, while EBITDA excludes Mattress Firm. The issuer's 2.31x covenant ratio for that date nets USD 1,592.3 million of the escrow cash and gives net debt of USD 2,134.8 million against USD 3,692.5 million on unrestricted cash, so the two year-end series should not be compared with the 2026 figures without that adjustment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mix of claims has shifted toward unsecured debt. Senior unsecured principal is USD 3,100.0 million at 2026-09-30, 55.09% of principal of USD 5,627.0 million against 33.92% at 2025-12-31, because the three Leggett & Platt notes of USD 500.0 million each came with the acquisition and carry no guarantee from Somnigroup's subsidiaries, while secured principal fell from USD 2,908.4 million to USD 2,329.3 million after the Amendment No. 5 refinancing and a USD 700.0 million Term B prepayment. Secured principal is 1.84x trailing reported EBITDA, down from 2.80x at 2025-12-31, which strengthens the secured lenders and leaves unsecured noteholders relying on cash flow rather than collateral; the Leggett & Platt notes are claims on that company alone. The earlier source review quoted total debt of USD 5,627.0 million, which is principal; the ratios in this module use carrying value of USD 5,381.6 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is adequate but will fall from its latest level. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 5.34x in FY2024, 3.73x in FY2025 and 5.01x over the trailing twelve months; the FY2025 low reflects cash interest of USD 278.3 million, up from USD 157.7 million, on the acquisition debt, and USD 266.7 million of acquisition-related charges that hold reported EBITDA below adjusted EBITDA, which covered cash interest 4.69x. Trailing cash interest of USD 252.7 million holds 36 days of interest on the Leggett & Platt notes, and the issuer's guide of about USD 240 million of cash interest for 2026, raised from about USD 225 million in the annual report, implies USD 68.5 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 57.17 million in the first three, the first quarter to carry those notes for a full period, so run-rate cover will be below 5.01x even allowing for the uneven timing of semi-annual note interest.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the strongest part of the credit. Operating cash flow was USD 831.9 million in nine months 2026 against USD 700.7 million a year earlier and, after USD 174.3 million of capital expenditure, free cash flow was USD 657.6 million, or USD 698.7 million over the trailing twelve months, which is 0.55x trailing EBITDA. Its quality is mixed: a USD 135.5 million release from working capital supplied 16.29% of operating cash flow, deferred taxes added USD 49.4 million without cash, and capital expenditure is guided to about USD 255 million for 2026 including USD 75 million of one-time Mattress Firm store refresh. After dividends of USD 108.1 million, free cash flow of USD 549.5 million funded most of the USD 583.9 million of net debt repayment, while the cash balance rose to USD 612.1 million mainly because Leggett & Platt brought USD 560.2 million of cash.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is ample for the debt falling due soon. It was USD 1,794.8 million at 2026-09-30, made of USD 612.1 million of cash and USD 1,182.7 million of revolver availability, compared with USD 773.6 million at 2025-12-31. The revolver is the only undrawn facility because the securitization is fully drawn at USD 100.5 million, and USD 200.0 million of the cash went to the Term B prepayment the next day. By final maturity, debt falls due USD 600.5 million in 2027, USD 1,300.0 million in 2029 and USD 3,028.8 million in 2031; the 2027 amount is the securitization due 2027-10-07 and the USD 500.0 million Leggett & Platt note due 2027-11-15, and liquidity covers it 2.99 times. The ladder uses final maturities only, so term loan amortisation, which the filings do not quantify, would bring part of the 2031 amount forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 55, 100; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 23, 47; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Obligations outside total debt are material. Operating lease obligations are USD 2,143.2 million, pension payments of USD 33.0 million and letters of credit of USD 34.8 million were scheduled at 2025-12-31 with no purchase commitments listed, and about USD 110.0 million of accounts payable, 12.67% of the USD 868.4 million total, is settled through third-party supplier payment programmes that the company uses following the Leggett & Platt acquisition. The filing states that the company pays the provider on the original invoice due date and cannot lengthen payment terms through the programmes, so the amount adds no obligation beyond ordinary payables, but it is a dependence on third-party finance whose size, with no earlier figure to compare, should be tracked. No lease-adjusted leverage is stated because operating lease cost is already deducted in EBITDA, and adding the lease obligations to debt without adding the rent back would count the lease twice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 103; calculation C1; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Underlying trading is soft, which weakens the earnings that must carry the debt. Net sales were USD 2,350.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, 10.75% above the third quarter of 2025, but USD 1,978.2 million without the USD 372.6 million from Leggett & Platt, down 6.80%, with Mattress Firm and North America each down 5.8% and International down 12.3% after an ERP implementation disrupted Dreams. Gross margin fell to 42.02% from 44.89% because Leggett & Platt's 17.7% margin dilutes the mix, and North America's margin gain of 6.3 percentage points includes about USD 20.0 million of tariff refunds that may not repeat. Add-backs were 16.16% of adjusted EBITDA in the quarter against 9.52% a year earlier, so adjusted EBITDA of USD 447.5 million flatters reported EBITDA of USD 375.2 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 35–36, 51–52; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The covenant measure does not show that earnings support the debt. The issuer's covenant leverage was 2.31x at FY2024, 3.21x at FY2025 and 2.69x at 2026-09-30 against a 5.00x maximum, but the 2026 figure rests on EBITDA of USD 1,864.8 million: adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,389.3 million plus USD 330.5 million of Leggett & Platt earnings before acquisition and USD 145.0 million of expected cost synergies. Those additions are 34.23% of adjusted EBITDA. The filings print the level of only one of the three maintenance tests, so headroom on the interest coverage and secured net leverage tests is not assessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63, 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 52–53; calculation C18; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a leverage concern is the issuer's covenant leverage of 2.69x against a 5.00x maximum, trailing free cash flow of USD 698.7 million, liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million and no note or facility final maturity before 2027. If Leggett & Platt earns close to the USD 330.5 million the issuer adds back for the part of the year it did not own, full-period leverage would move toward the issuer's target range of 2.0x to 3.0x and the comfort would rest on earnings as well as cash. The view would turn toward comfort on a printed full-period EBITDA for Leggett & Platt, two quarters of positive net sales growth excluding acquisitions, or debt repayment beyond the USD 200.0 million Term B prepayment. It would turn toward concern if the third-quarter softness at Mattress Firm and International persists as the 2027 maturities approach, or if add-backs keep rising as a share of adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact pack for Somnigroup International Inc. (formerly Tempur Sealy International, Inc.) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and financial-policy behaviour, the Mattress Firm and Leggett & Platt acquisitions and the related financing, and issuer history, from the five supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used and no web search was made. The run settings were read as the user's dated inputs, not as evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Somnigroup is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder named in its filings, so creditors rely on its own financial policy, and two acquisitions since 2025-02-05, funded by debt and shares, show that policy has favoured scale over deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisitions lifted net sales from USD 4,930.9 million in FY2024 to USD 7,844.2 million over the trailing twelve months and total debt from USD 3,809.9 million to USD 5,381.6 million, while dividends stayed small at USD 108.1 million in nine months 2026 and no shares were repurchased under the programme. The main risks are integration of Leggett & Platt, whose gross margin is 17.7% against 42.02% for the group, and a Mattress Firm segment whose net sales fell 5.8% in the third quarter; the filings name no sponsor fees, related-party payments or creditor-adverse transactions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 9, 19, 35–36; calculation C1; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is now a vertically integrated bedding group in which company-owned stores are the largest route to the consumer, which ties cash flow to consumer traffic but not to any one customer. Direct sales were 63.48% of net sales in FY2025 against 24.93% in FY2024 because Mattress Firm is a retailer, and the group states that no customer exceeds 5% of global sales. The store network carries operating lease cost of USD 489.5 million, 6.55% of FY2025 net sales, so a fall in traffic cuts earnings faster than sales, and Mattress Firm net sales fell 5.8% in the third quarter of 2026 on softer online sales with slightly lower same-store sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; calculation C8; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition policy, not sponsor behaviour, is the main driver of creditor risk. Total debt rose USD 1,571.7 million, 41.25%, between 2024-12-31 and 2026-09-30, while net sales over the trailing twelve months were 59.08% above FY2024. Mattress Firm cost USD 5,408.4 million, of which 57.16% was cash and 41.51% shares, and the USD 2,896.5 million drawn or released from escrow at closing, equal to 93.69% of that cash, also had to repay Mattress Firm's debt and pay fees; Leggett & Platt cost USD 1,289.6 million, 98.78% in shares, but it brought USD 1,500.0 million of notes with it. The second deal therefore added less new borrowing but the same direction of travel, and the issuer's own leverage target of 2.0x to 3.0x is on the covenant measure, not on reported earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17, 19, 21, 45; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to lean on and none to fear, so support for creditors cannot be inferred from who owns the company. The filings name no controlling holder and no sponsor, and the new shares issued to the sellers of the two acquired companies equal 23.50% of shares outstanding on 2026-11-04. The equity cushion is thinner than it looks: goodwill and intangible assets of USD 7,608.4 million exceed stockholders' equity of USD 4,633.6 million, so tangible equity is negative USD 2,974.8 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 6–7, 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; calculation C4; calculation C10; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions are modest and growing, and no leverage test in the debt documents currently stops them. The dividend per share rose from USD 0.44 in 2023 to USD 0.52 in 2024 and USD 0.60 in 2025 and is USD 0.17 a quarter in 2026, USD 0.68 a year, and the USD 108.1 million paid in nine months 2026 was 12.99% of operating cash flow. No shares were repurchased under the programme in 2025 or 2026, with USD 774.5 million of authorisation unused. The issuer's covenant ratio of 2.69x is below both the 3.75x and 3.50x levels under which restricted payments are unlimited, so restraint is the board's choice, and the builder basket grows by 50% of adjusted net income each quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is timely, audited and detailed on covenants, but control coverage of the acquired businesses is incomplete. The annual report was signed 58 days after year-end with an unqualified audit opinion, and the third-quarter report 40 days after quarter-end with a quarterly covenant reconciliation. Mattress Firm's internal controls are still being brought into the assessment for 2026, Leggett & Platt is excluded from that assessment, and the Dreams ERP system went live in the third quarter with modified controls while Dreams net sales fell 34.7%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Integration evidence is positive at Mattress Firm and unproven at Leggett & Platt. The covenant add-back for expected Mattress Firm cost savings fell from USD 100.0 million at FY2025 to USD 70.0 million at 2026-09-30, and the issuer states that Mattress Firm synergies added 420 bp to North America gross margin in the third quarter and 570 bp over nine months, so those savings are being realised; the USD 75.0 million Leggett & Platt add-back is unrealised and its stub gross margin is 17.7%. Excluding Leggett & Platt, adjusted operating income fell 5.91% in the third quarter, and pro forma net sales including Leggett & Platt fell 6.30%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 33, 36, 41, 49–53; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leggett & Platt's debt is structurally separate, so which creditors stand where cannot be established from these filings. Its three notes of USD 1,500.0 million carry no guarantee and are obligations of Leggett & Platt, Incorporated, while the guarantors of the credit facilities and of the 2029 and 2031 notes are not named; the company is designated a restricted subsidiary, which brings its earnings into the covenant measure. Whether its assets support the secured facilities or the other notes is not stated, and that question decides how the added debt ranks against the existing creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading acquisition appetite as a creditor risk is that Leggett & Platt was 98.78% paid in shares, that the filings show no debt-funded distribution or sponsor extraction, that the issuer reports covenant leverage of 2.69x against a 2.0x to 3.0x target, and that the Mattress Firm synergy add-back has fallen by USD 30.0 million as savings were achieved. The view would improve on a printed full-period result for Leggett & Platt that supports the USD 330.5 million pre-acquisition add-back, on a guarantor list showing the new subsidiaries stand behind the senior secured and note creditors, and on continued debt repayment ahead of dividends. It would worsen on another debt-funded acquisition, on a rise in distributions while reported leverage stays high, or if third-quarter sales weakness at Mattress Firm and International continues.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16, 45, 47, 52–53; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no sponsor or controlling holder exists rests on the filings naming none; a large holder, board control rights or related-party fees would change the ownership and governance reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the conclusion that no leverage test restrains distributions rests on the issuer's summary; baskets, carve-outs and unrestricted-subsidiary capacity could change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leggett & Platt appears for 36 days only, so the reading of that segment's margin, customers and savings is provisional until a full quarter is reported.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The finding that Mattress Firm savings are being realised rests on a margin effect stated in basis points and a falling add-back, because no filing prints a savings target or a dollar amount realised to date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The statement that no customer exceeds 5% of global sales dates from the annual report before Leggett & Platt, so low customer dependence is not yet shown for its automotive, furniture and industrial customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The two acquisitions since 2025-02-05 define the credit. Mattress Firm closed on 2025-02-05 for total consideration of USD 5,408.4 million: USD 3,091.5 million of cash, USD 2,245.1 million of shares at USD 65.65 each and USD 71.8 million of settled pre-existing balances, less USD 267.0 million of cash acquired. The cash was funded by USD 625.0 million of the Delayed Draw Term A Loan, USD 679.5 million of revolver borrowing and about USD 1,592.0 million of Term B Loan proceeds released from escrow, where they had been held since 2024-10-24, and the same proceeds also repaid Mattress Firm's debt and paid fees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leggett & Platt closed on 2026-08-26 for total consideration of USD 1,289.6 million, almost all in new shares valued at USD 64.09 each, with net consideration of USD 730.0 million after USD 560.2 million of cash acquired; its three senior notes of USD 500.0 million each remain outstanding at Leggett & Platt, Incorporated with no guarantee, and the debt assumed was recorded at USD 1,283.6 million. No new bonds were issued in either transaction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financing around the second deal was a refinancing, not new money for the purchase. Amendment No. 5 of 2026-07-27 added a USD 1,200.0 million Term A Loan and USD 510.0 million of revolving commitments, took revolver commitments to USD 1,700.0 million, extended both to 2031-07-27, and repaid the earlier term loans, and USD 700.0 million of the Term B Loan was prepaid with the remaining proceeds. A further USD 200.0 million of the Term B Loan was prepaid on 2026-10-01 with cash acquired and cash from operations, after the balance-sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by an acquisition-led financial policy and unresolved ownership, guarantor and basket information, because those facts raise leverage and leave the creditor protections untested, which implies a higher monitoring burden. Countervailing evidence is the share funding of the second deal, the cash-funded Term B prepayments and the modest dividend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Somnigroup International Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope: business and financial profile, ownership and financial policy, outlook, an issuer-specific downside scenario, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers, drawn from the five supplied filings and the earlier modules' findings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external sources were used and no web search was made. The run settings were read as the user's dated inputs, not as evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is adequate but stretched: cash generation and liquidity support USD 5,381.6 million of debt, yet reported leverage of 4.25x, falling organic sales and unproven Leggett & Platt integration leave little room for another acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main support is free cash flow of USD 698.7 million over the trailing twelve months and liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million against USD 600.5 million of debt maturing in 2027. The primary downside is a further fall in consumer demand reaching fixed store and plant costs as the 2027 maturities approach; the issuer's 2.69x covenant ratio does not measure that risk, because it adds USD 475.5 million of EBITDA beyond adjusted earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and channel breadth are real strengths but are being diluted by lower-margin acquired earnings. The group has four segments, direct sales of 54.44% of net sales in the third quarter of 2026 and no customer above 5% of global sales before Leggett & Platt, which spreads demand risk across stores, wholesale partners and now components. Leggett & Platt earns a gross margin of 17.71% against 42.02% for the group, so each acquired dollar of sales carries less margin to service debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 35–36; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the strongest support. Trailing operating cash flow of USD 931.3 million less capital expenditure of USD 232.6 million leaves free cash flow of USD 698.7 million, 0.55x trailing EBITDA, and dividends of USD 108.1 million in nine months 2026 took 16.44% of nine-month free cash flow. Capital expenditure and the dividend are the levers management controls, so the cash flow can protect creditors in a downturn if they are used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the weakest dimension, and the range of credible answers is wide. Reported total debt to EBITDA is 4.25x and net debt to EBITDA 3.77x, also 3.77x pro forma for the USD 200.0 million Term B prepayment of 2026-10-01, while the issuer's covenant ratio is 2.69x. The reported figures overstate leverage because Leggett & Platt's debt is counted against 36 days of its earnings; the covenant ratio understates it because its EBITDA is 34.23% above adjusted EBITDA, and no source gives a full-period figure between the two.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 52–54; calculation C1; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the debt calendar are comfortable for the next two years. Liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million is made of USD 612.1 million of cash, USD 412.1 million after the USD 200.0 million prepayment of 2026-10-01, and USD 1,182.7 million of revolver availability; it covers the 2027 maturities 2.99 times. The bank debt now matures in 2031, so the next test of market access is the USD 500.0 million Leggett & Platt note due 2027-11-15 and the securitization due 2027-10-07.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21, 47; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cost is likely to rise as a share of cash flow, and a rising rate would add to it. The issuer's guide of about USD 240 million of cash interest for 2026 implies USD 68.5 million in the fourth quarter against an average of USD 57.17 million in the first three, and 43.11% of principal is floating rate, so 100 bp costs about USD 24.3 million a year, 3.48% of trailing free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 47, 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings momentum is negative and is the main reason the credit is stretched. Net sales excluding Leggett & Platt fell 6.80% in the third quarter of 2026, pro forma net sales including it fell 6.30%, and adjusted operating income excluding it fell 5.91%, with Mattress Firm and North America each down 5.8% and International down 12.3%. A fixed cost base of stores, plants and leases, of which operating lease cost alone was USD 489.5 million in FY2025, turns that fall into a larger fall in EBITDA, which is why interest cover and leverage are sensitive to a further weak quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 34–36, 49–51; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 103; calculation C5; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is acquisitive and the equity cushion is thin, so creditor protection rests on restraint rather than structure. Total debt rose USD 1,571.7 million, 41.25%, since 2024-12-31, goodwill and intangibles exceed stockholders' equity so tangible equity is negative USD 2,974.8 million, and the unsecured share of principal rose to 55.09% with USD 1,500.0 million of Leggett & Platt notes that carry no guarantee. No sponsor exists to inject equity, and the guarantors are not named, so the priority of the new debt against the older creditors is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the stretched view is that the issuer reports covenant leverage of 2.69x against a 5.00x maximum, that nine-month free cash flow covers the dividend 6.08 times, that Leggett & Platt was paid for mainly in shares, and that Mattress Firm synergies added 420 bp to North America gross margin in the quarter. The view would move toward strong on a printed full-period EBITDA for Leggett & Platt near the USD 330.5 million pre-acquisition add-back, two quarters of net sales growth excluding acquisitions, and repayment of the 2027 maturities from cash flow. It would move toward weak if third-quarter sales declines persist, if the add-backs rise further, or if another debt-funded acquisition is announced before leverage returns to the issuer's 2.0x to 3.0x target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 36, 45, 47, 52–53; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C6

fields.value: - A full-period EBITDA for Leggett & Platt is not printed, so the leverage assessment stays a range between the reported and covenant figures and the weak rating of leverage could improve if that earnings figure is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is cash generation. Trailing free cash flow of USD 698.7 million, 0.55x EBITDA, is large enough to fund the dividend of USD 108.1 million and net repayment of USD 583.9 million of credit facilities in nine months, so deleveraging does not depend on market access. This lowers refinancing risk but is only as durable as sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is liquidity and tenor. Liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million covers the USD 600.5 million due in 2027 2.99 times, and the bank facilities run to 2031, so a failed refinancing of the 2027 items would not force a liquidity crisis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 47; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is scale and channel breadth: four segments, brands across price points, direct sales of 54.44% of the third quarter, and no customer above 5% of global sales before Leggett & Platt, which spreads demand risk and supports pricing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is leverage on reported earnings, 4.25x total debt to EBITDA, with the full-period figure not printed; it limits headroom for a downturn or another acquisition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is falling underlying sales, down 6.80% in the third quarter excluding Leggett & Platt, with fixed store and plant costs that magnify the fall in EBITDA and so raise leverage and lower cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is earnings quality and integration: add-backs are 16.16% of adjusted EBITDA in the quarter and the covenant measure adds USD 475.5 million, including USD 145.0 million of unrealised savings, so reported compliance is a weak signal of cash earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is structure and policy: the unsecured share of principal is 55.09%, USD 1,500.0 million of notes sit at Leggett & Platt without guarantees, guarantors are not named and tangible equity is negative USD 2,974.8 million, so priority and loss absorption for lenders are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C8; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Somnigroup designs, manufactures, distributes and retails bedding through Tempur Sealy, Mattress Firm and Dreams and, since 2026-08-26, makes engineered components through Leggett & Platt. Direct sales were 63.48% of FY2025 net sales against 24.93% in FY2024 because Mattress Firm is a retailer, and the second acquisition adds a component business with a lower gross margin and different end markets. Store-based sales and component supply are discretionary and cyclical, so cash-flow visibility is moderate: modest seasonality and the absence of customer concentration help, while store leases and plant costs make earnings sensitive to demand, which matters for debt service and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 11, 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 30–31; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is listed with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings and a fully-owned group of operating businesses plus 50.0% joint ventures that are equity accounted. Sellers of the two acquired companies hold new shares equal to 23.50% of shares outstanding, which links part of the owner base to the integration outcome. Because no sponsor exists, support in a stress cannot be assumed and the creditor claim rests on the group's own cash flow; the guarantor perimeter and the restricted group are not described beyond a general statement, so structural priority between the secured facilities, the Somnigroup notes and the Leggett & Platt notes needs a separate review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 10; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is driven by consumer traffic and mix in Mattress Firm, wholesale partner orders in North America and International, and by component demand at Leggett & Platt. Third-quarter net sales excluding Leggett & Platt fell 6.80%, led by a 12.3% fall at International after the Dreams system change and a 5.8% fall at Mattress Firm and North America, while gross margin rose in North America on synergies and about USD 20.0 million of tariff refunds. Revenue is cyclical and discretionary rather than contracted, with limited visibility; the group has taken pricing actions against tariffs, but the North America margin gain includes refunds that may not repeat, so the sales trend, not price, decides cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of sales is 57.4% of FY2025 net sales and selling and marketing 23.3%, with store occupancy and manufacturing depreciation inside cost of sales and operating lease cost of USD 489.5 million, so a large part of the cost base is fixed in the short run. Group gross margin fell to 42.02% from 44.89% in the third quarter because Leggett & Platt's margin is lower, and raw material and tariff exposure remains, although most U.S. sales are of U.S.-made product. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through savings already visible at Mattress Firm, but a larger fall in volume would deleverage stores and plants and lower EBITDA faster than sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 48, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 35–36; calculation C5; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital expenditure is 2.92% of nine-month net sales and guided to about USD 255 million for 2026 including USD 75 million of one-time store refresh, so it is moderate and partly discretionary. Trailing free cash flow is 0.55x EBITDA after cash interest of USD 252.7 million, working capital release supplied 16.29% of nine-month operating cash flow and integration costs recur with each deal. EBITDA turns into free cash flow reliably enough to fund the dividend and debt repayment, but part of the conversion rests on working capital and on add-backs that need cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_sgi.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 44; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high: domestic manufacturing is concentrated but retail is fragmented, competition is on price, brand and availability, and online direct-to-consumer entrants and retailer private labels press margins. Buyer power is moderated by direct ownership of the largest specialty retailer and the absence of customers above 5% of sales, while supplier power is limited because the group buys from several suppliers and now makes components itself. For creditors the force that matters is rivalry in a weak market, which caps pricing and makes volume recovery the route to margin repair.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Consumer confidence, housing activity, interest rates and tariffs are primary credit drivers: the issuer says the bedding industry was challenged in 2025 and remains pressured in 2026, interest rates remain relatively high, and tariff policy is uncertain, although the group expects no material tariff effect on 2026 results. These factors reach the credit through consumer traffic and through the floating-rate share of debt of 43.11%, so a weak consumer and higher rates would pressure sales and interest cost together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the cash flow, liquidity and tenor, and the breadth of brands and channels. Weaknesses are leverage on reported earnings, falling underlying sales and thin tangible equity. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Mattress Firm and Leggett & Platt savings, with USD 145.0 million of covenant add-backs still unrealised, and repayment of the remaining Term B Loan from cash flow. Threats that could weaken it are a prolonged consumer downturn, a further debt-funded acquisition, tariff changes and a delay in refinancing the 2027 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the issuer expects capital expenditure of about USD 255 million and cash interest of about USD 240 million for 2026 and a leverage target of 2.0x to 3.0x on the covenant measure; the filings give no sales or earnings guidance. Tailwinds are the savings still to come, the lower margin on refinanced debt and, in the issuer's view, long-term industry growth from consumer awareness of sleep and housing formations; headwinds are weak consumer demand, a fourth-quarter interest cost above the first three quarters' average, Leggett & Platt's lower margin and a 2027 maturity cluster. Over three to five years, deleveraging depends on volume recovery and on discipline over further acquisitions, which cannot be assessed from the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a further weakening of U.S. consumer demand while Dreams recovers slowly. The first operational break is lower traffic and same-store sales at Mattress Firm and lower wholesale orders at North America, where the third-quarter fall of 5.8% in each already shows the direction, and Leggett & Platt's furniture, flooring and automotive customers would add cyclical exposure. Fixed store, plant and lease costs, of which lease cost alone is USD 489.5 million, would turn the sales fall into a larger fall in EBITDA, free cash flow of USD 698.7 million would shrink, and reported leverage of 4.25x would rise. Liquidity of USD 1,794.8 million, the capital expenditure guide of about USD 255 million and the dividend of USD 108.1 million in nine months are the levers, and the next observable tests are quarterly net sales excluding acquisitions, revolver borrowings of USD 516.5 million, the covenant ratio and the refinancing of the securitization and the Leggett & Platt note due in 2027. On the evidence, liquidity distress within 24 months is not indicated because liquidity covers the 2027 maturities 2.99 times, but the leverage reduction the issuer targets would be pushed back.

fields.value: Overall, Somnigroup presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands, channel breadth and strong cash generation, but credit quality is constrained by leverage on reported earnings, falling underlying sales and a thin equity cushion. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers dividends and capital expenditure but depends on demand. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the integration of Leggett & Platt, the 2027 maturities and the covenant EBITDA add-backs. The primary downside path is weaker consumer demand acting on fixed store and plant costs. Further analysis would require a full-period EBITDA for Leggett & Platt, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement. Fundamental credit analysis completed with limitations. Top risk: sales decline against a fixed cost base while leverage is high.
